title: Preface
summary:
The partial document is a service report for Maple Ridge Transit Authority for the year 2025. It covers the following main points:
1. Authority Overview
2. Route Network
3. Ridership and Fares
4. Fleet Electrification
5. Accessibility
6. On-Time Performance

title: Authority Overview
summary: The main points covered in the partial document are the operations of the transit authority in Maple Ridge, including the number of buses and routes, the establishment year, and details about the depots and control center locations.

title: Route Network
summary: The partial document covers the core network consisting of twelve high-frequency routes and twenty-two local routes. It highlights the busiest routes in 2025, including their average weekday ridership and midday scheduled headway. The document also mentions Route 3, which connects the university campus with the central station and is limited in capacity due to a bridge span that restricts vehicle length to 12 meters. A table lists the top seven busiest routes with their ridership and headway times.

title: Ridership and Fares
summary: The partial document covers ridership and fares for a transportation system. It mentions that total ridership in 2025 was 41.2 million rides, a 4 percent increase from 2024. The document also notes that weekday boardings peaked between 7:30 and 8:30 in the morning. Fares include a single fare of 2.75 CAD and a monthly pass costing 96 CAD. Additionally, it states that children under 12 travel free and that there is an employer partnership programme covering 34,000 pass holders.

title: Fleet Electrification
summary: The partial document covers fleet electrification efforts, including the number of battery electric buses by December 2025, the number of fast chargers at different depots, the authority's goal of achieving a fully zero emission fleet by 2035, and how winter range loss affects the use of electric buses on route 34, necessitating the use of diesel buses as reserves.

title: Accessibility
summary:
The partial document covers accessibility features of a bus fleet. Key points include:
- 92 percent of bus stops are wheelchair accessible with level boarding or a raised pad.
- All buses in the fleet have either ramps or kneeling suspension.
- The failure rate of ramps in daily service was 0.7 percent in 2025.
- Audio-visual next stop announcements are installed in 84 percent of the fleet and are mandatory for all new vehicles.

title: On-Time Performance
summary: The partial document covers on-time performance metrics for a system, showing a 87.3% on-time departure rate in 2025. It also identifies congestion and traffic incidents as primary causes of delays, accounting for 54% and 21% respectively. The document highlights that the bridge approach of Route 3 has the poorest on-time performance during the afternoon peak, with an 87.3% drop to 71%.
